findings.statement: a log-only durable batch clears the registered floor band on this host
findings.detail: raw append + fdatasync sustains 1191125 ops/s at batch 1000 (0.84ms per barrier). The registered band is 600k-2.5M; below it a one-barrier commit cannot beat LMDB's recorded 572,416 ops/s and the redesign's durable-load promise dies here, above it the fsync is suspect and needs O_DSYNC scrutiny before belief

findings.statement: memtable bookkeeping costs under 20% of the raw floor
findings.detail: raw+index 1014003 ops/s against raw 1191125 (raw+index vs raw: less 0.851x (p=0.0298, rel_iqr 10.1%/14.1%)), keeping 85.1%. Failing means the memtable, not the log, is the next engine's write-path problem

findings.statement: today's engine sits 3-8x below the one-barrier floor
findings.detail: supdb 203603 ops/s against the raw floor's 1191125 -- 5.85x below (raw vs supdb: greater 5.850x (p=0.0022, rel_iqr 14.1%/5.9%)). This gap is what a WAL-only engine claims to recover; under 3x the rewrite buys little on this axis, over 8x the per-point work is worse than EXT.9's decomposition suggests

notes: three arms interleaved in one process, fresh file per rep, the EXT.9 load shape: every key new, a durability point every batch. raw-wal is write_all + fdatasync of the framed batch and nothing else; raw+index adds a hash-map insert per op; supdb is put + checkpoint under the shipped value-carrying log
predictions registered in walfloor-plan.md before the first full run. EXT.9's recorded lmdb 572,416 ops/s is context only -- no finding compares across runs
